topic: What if you brought a modern car to ancient Rome?

script.text: Eight forty in the morning. You've had your driver's license for exactly three days. Your best friend Mo is in the passenger seat, picking the music. You drive into a tunnel.
Halfway through, the radio turns to static. The lights in the tunnel flicker. Then there's a flash, so bright you have to shut your eyes.
When you open them, the road is gone. You're on a dirt track, in blazing sun. A man with a donkey stares at you. Then he drops everything and runs.
Your GPS says, 'Recalculating.' Then it says nothing at all.
Mo points. Across the hills there's an aqueduct. A huge one. And behind it, a city of white marble.
What if you brought a modern car to ancient Rome?
For a few days, you'll be the most powerful person in the world. But every kilometer you drive costs something you can never get back.
